description: Resolve one drug name to its FDA identity, then fan out in parallel across the bounded per-drug openFDA endpoints and merge into one profile: identity, label highlights, adverse-event summary, recall history, Drugs@FDA approval, and shortage status. Identity and label come from an original packager's label when one matches (identity.is_original_packager says when they do not), approval is the drug's own application ranked over its Drugs@FDA matches, and each section names the product it describes. Replaces chaining openfda_get_drug_label, openfda_search_adverse_events, openfda_search_recalls, openfda_search_drug_approvals, and openfda_search_drug_shortages — and reconciles the identifier drift between endpoints that makes that chaining error-prone. Each section is best-effort: a miss returns null rather than failing the call, and a sub-query the 50 s profile deadline cuts is listed in degraded. For deep dives into any one area, use the dedicated tool.

drug.description: Drug name to profile — brand or generic (e.g. "metformin", "Humira", "Glucophage"). Resolved once to an FDA identity. The Drugs@FDA approval is ranked over this name's matches; meta.fanOutKey reports the name the recall and shortage sub-queries searched.

name: openfda_drug_profile

seriousCount.description: Reports flagged serious (serious=1). total − seriousCount covers both non-serious reports and those with no seriousness recorded.

items.description: A reaction term paired with its report count.

total.description: Adverse-event reports naming this drug — every matching report, including those with no seriousness recorded; equals openfda_search_adverse_events meta.total for the same medicinalproduct search.

adverse_events.description: Adverse-event summary aggregated over drug/event, or null when unavailable.

applicationNumber.description: NDA, ANDA, or BLA application number.

brandNames.description: Brand names of the application's products (products.brand_name).

candidates.description: Drugs@FDA applications the ranked search matched. Above 100, only the first 100 were ranked, and a notice says so.

approval.description: The drug's own Drugs@FDA application, ranked over up to 100 matches of the input name: NDA and BLA applications by openfda.generic_name or products.active_ingredients.name, and any application whose products.brand_name is the name. Ranked on each application's own products: a brand name equal to the input that is not an ingredient name, then one ingredient (several when the name is a combination), then an ingredient without a biologic suffix, then reference_drug Yes, then NDA or BLA, then marketed over discontinued over tentative, then the lowest application number. When the name matches none, the same rank runs over meta.fanOutKey's openfda.generic_name and products.active_ingredients.name matches. Null when nothing matched or the search failed (listed in degraded).

degraded.description: Sub-queries that failed upstream, empty when every section resolved. A section listed here is unknown, not absent — a null section with no entry here genuinely has no FDA record.

items.description: One failed sub-query and why it failed.

message.description: Upstream failure message for this section, truncated.

reason.description: Machine-readable failure reason (e.g. rate_limited, upstream_error, query_error, or timeout when the profile deadline cut the request).

error.description: Present when the call failed. Absent on success.

code.description: JSON-RPC error code for this failure.

reason.description: Machine-readable failure mode. Declared by this tool: `blank_drug_name`: The drug name carries no searchable character — only quotes, backslashes, or whitespace. Other values are possible when a failure originates below the handler.

recovery.description: Actionable next step for the caller.

message.description: Human-readable description of what went wrong.

identity.description: Identity of one product: an original packager's drug/label record matching the name, else any label matching the name, else a drug/ndc record — replaced by the approval application's own original-packager label whenever the record found is not it.

application_number.description: Application (NDA, ANDA, BLA) the resolved label or NDC record is filed under. When it differs from approval.applicationNumber, identity and label describe another product than approval does.

brand_names.description: Brand names on the resolved record: a label's openfda.brand_name, or the drug/ndc record's brand_name.

generic_name.description: Generic name (openfda.generic_name) of the resolved label or NDC record — it can name one product (e.g. "ADALIMUMAB-AACF" on a biosimilar's label). meta.fanOutKey uses it unless the input term is whole words of it.

is_original_packager.description: True when openFDA flags the resolved record as the original packager's (openfda.is_original_packager). False for a harmonized record openFDA leaves unflagged, as a repackager's or relabeler's is. Null when openFDA harmonized nothing for the record.

manufacturer.description: Manufacturer on the resolved label (openfda.manufacturer_name), or the drug/ndc record's labeler.

rxcui.description: RxNorm concept unique identifier, when available.

spl_set_id.description: SPL set ID for the drug label, when available.

warnings.description: Warnings (truncated) — boxed warning or warnings_and_cautions for Rx labels, falling back to the OTC-monograph warnings section.

label.description: Label highlights from the drug/label record identity was resolved from, or null when no label matched.

drug.description: The drug name supplied in the request, echoed back.

fanOutKey.description: Name the recall/enforcement and shortage sub-queries ran against, and the Drugs@FDA approval search when the input name matches no application — the input term when it is whole words of the resolved generic name (an ingredient such as "metformin" or "adalimumab", so one label's product-specific generic does not narrow them), otherwise the resolved generic name, falling back to a brand name, then the input term. Derived from the label the name itself matched, before any swap to the approval's own label. The adverse-event sub-queries instead key off the raw input term to match heterogeneous reporter-entered values.

resolvedVia.description: Which endpoint resolved the canonical identity: drug/label, drug/ndc, or none.

notice.description: Guidance when the drug could not be resolved, upstream errors degraded the profile, a failed label lookup left another label shown, or the approval ranking or shortage counts covered only the first 100 matches. Absent otherwise.

recalls.description: The newest 5 drug/enforcement recall actions whose openfda.generic_name or product_description matches meta.fanOutKey (may be empty); recalls_total counts every match.

items.description: A single recall or enforcement action.

recalls_total.description: Total drug/enforcement reports the recall search matched — recalls lists the newest 5 of them. Null when the recall sub-query failed (listed in degraded): unknown, not zero.

sectionsFound.description: How many profile sections (label, adverse_events, recalls, approval, shortage) returned data.

namesInput.description: True when the shown record names the input drug, by product or presentation, or the input itself keyed the search. False for brand input no record names: the record shown is the newest for meta.fanOutKey, another product's.

presentation.description: Presentation the shown record covers: product, dosage form, strength, NDC.

product.description: Product the shown record covers: its openfda.brand_name, else its presentation's lead.

status.description: Status of the shown record (Current, To Be Discontinued, or Resolved) — one presentation, not the whole drug; statusCounts tallies every record.

statusCounts.description: Records per status over the newest 100 matches, most frequent first.

items.description: A status paired with its record count.

total.description: Shortage records whose generic_name matches meta.fanOutKey.

shortage.description: One drug/shortages record for meta.fanOutKey — for brand input, the newest naming the brand, else the newest — with the product, company, and presentation it covers, the match total, and per-status counts. Null when none on record or the search failed (listed in degraded).

title: Openfda Drug Profile
